What is e-BASA?

e-BASA is an easy-to-use, teacher-supported reading application that helps learners read, practise and grow as readers, even without an internet connection. It gives learners original fables and stories written in a big-book style, audio-assisted pronunciation, word-meaning support and games, and it gives teachers a simple way to monitor each learner’s reading progress. The “e” stands for “electronic”: e-BASA is a digital reading helper with one aim: every child a reader.

What is new in version 3.0

  • BULIG and BASA GO! are now inside e-BASA. One app now holds the 62 BULIG Level 4 Fluency Toolkit passages and the official Phil-IRI English passages (Grades 2–6), together with the 60 original stories. Use the Source filter in Story Time to show one set at a time.
  • Phil-IRI tab in the Teacher Corner: score a passage, Screening test (GST), Class record (Form 2), Learner record (Form 4), official passages, printable forms 1–4 and a next-step advisor. Reports keep e-BASA reading and Phil-IRI results separate.
  • A real dictionary: the Word Helper now has about 7,190 words with parts of speech, verb and plural forms, example sentences and Filipino and Bisaya meanings. Look up “went” or “babies” and it shows the base word (“go”, “baby”).
  • Comprehension Check and Game Pass for every story that has questions, with stars and reading ranks.
  • Phone version: a single web file that opens in a phone browser. READ TO ME re-syncs the highlighted word every sentence and scrolls along with it.
  • Printed companions: the e-BASA Story Book and User Manual (with a full-dictionary edition) and two pupil Word Helper dictionary books (English to Bisaya and Filipino; Bisaya to English and Filipino).

The projects behind e-BASA

  • BASA Pangantucan: the local reading advocacy that e-BASA was made in support of.
  • BULIG: the Division-wide reading program of the Division of Bukidnon. Its Level 4 Fluency Toolkit passages are included here for classroom practice.
  • BASA GO!: the companion reading app from which the BULIG toolkit and the Phil-IRI features come.
  • Phil-IRI: the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory of the Department of Education. The official English passages, screening test and forms are included as a teacher tool.

The BULIG and Phil-IRI materials belong to their respective DepEd programs and are included for the teacher’s own classroom use. e-BASA itself is a classroom helper and is not for submission or competition.

Original e-BASA passages

e-BASA has 60 original stories, ten for each grade from Grade 1 to Grade 6, written for this project in the style of big books: short, lively fables and tales with animal characters, repeated sounds and words, humor, a little mystery and a lesson at the end. They are told from the third-person point of view and are not copied from any book, program or toolkit. The BULIG and Phil-IRI passages are separate and are labelled by source. Their values include sharing, honesty, perseverance, teamwork, gratitude, kindness and love of reading and of nature. The title of each story is part of the text that learners read. Every story has comprehension questions (literal, inferential and critical) with suggested answers for the teacher. Teachers can add more passages in the Teacher Corner.

Key features

  • Story Time: grade-based passages from three sources (e-BASA, BULIG, Phil-IRI) with a Source filter, optional learner sign-in, and READ TO ME with PAUSE and STOP, word highlighting, five reading-speed levels and AUTO speed by grade
  • Comprehension Check: after each story, learners answer multiple-choice questions that are scored right away and earn ⭐ stars and reading ranks. (This is separate from the teacher’s oral comprehension questions in the Teacher Corner.)
  • Reading animations: a bouncing sound bar, a popping highlighted word and a little runner on the progress bar make Read to Me more lively
  • Word Helper (dictionary): about 7,190 words with parts of speech, verb and plural forms, examples, and English, Filipino and Bisaya meanings with SPEAK and SLOW; tap any word in a passage; teacher-added words
  • Reading Arcade: twelve passage-based games for words, vocabulary, spelling and blending, with stars, streaks and local scoreboards. A Game Pass, earned by reading stories and spending stars, unlocks one limited game round (3 stars, up to 10 questions, daily limit; teachers can change or switch off this rule)
  • Teacher Corner (PIN-protected): oral reading assessment with miscue tally and timer, comprehension questions, the Phil-IRI tab (scoring, GST, Forms 1–4), learner master list, school profile, analytics, research statistics, reading milestones, and printable reports
  • Usage monitoring: automatic logs of minutes, passages and games for each learner
  • Offline: runs without internet in regular use, on Windows, and as a web or phone app

Benefits

  • Gives learners entertaining stories they want to read again and again
  • Supports struggling readers and builds reading confidence
  • Saves teachers’ time in recording and summarising progress
  • Works offline, even in places with weak or no signal
  • Encourages families and communities to read together

Target beneficiaries

Learners in Grades 1 to 6, especially those who need more practice in reading fluently; teachers and school heads who monitor reading progress; and parents and community volunteers who support reading at home and in the barangay.

Project objectives

  1. Provide original, entertaining big-book style fables and stories for Grades 1–6 that learners can use offline.
  2. Encourage independent and repeated reading practice in school and at home.
  3. Provide pronunciation help through audio-assisted reading and word-meaning support in English, Filipino and Bisaya.
  4. Build vocabulary, spelling and word-recognition skills through games.
  5. Help teachers record, analyse and report learner reading progress at the beginning, middle and end of the school year.
  6. Help build a culture of reading in schools, homes and the community.

Reading progress monitoring

In the Teacher Corner, the teacher listens to a learner read a passage aloud, times the reading and tallies the miscues. e-BASA computes the oral reading score and reading speed, records the comprehension result, and shows the reading level: Independent (97–100%), Instructional (90–96%) or Frustration (89% and below). These are commonly used oral reading benchmarks; teachers should follow their school or division guidance if different cut-offs are required. Results can be tagged by period (BOSY, MOSY, EOSY or monitoring), compared in analytics and printed in printable reports. A reading milestone highlights learners who reach the criterion the teacher sets. The teacher remains responsible for the assessment, for interpreting results and for decisions about support.

Expected outputs and outcomes

  • A working offline reading companion with 60 original passages, plus the BULIG and Phil-IRI passages, for Grades 1–6
  • Audio-assisted pronunciation, word meanings and vocabulary games
  • A teacher-friendly progress-monitoring system with printable reports
  • More independent practice, better reading fluency and confidence, and better documentation of reading progress

Sustainability and expansion

The developer maintains e-BASA and adds passages and vocabulary based on classroom needs and feedback. Schools and districts that wish to use e-BASA can contact the developer. Headphones are recommended so that learners can listen without disturbing others.

Implementation guidelines for teachers

  1. Choose the learner’s grade and a passage in Story Time.
  2. Model the reading when needed, then let the learner listen and read along.
  3. Use the Word Helper to discuss new words in context.
  4. Encourage repeated reading and the Reading Arcade games.
  5. Use Teacher Corner → Assess a Learner for oral reading monitoring and the comprehension questions.
  6. Choose the period (BOSY, MOSY, EOSY or Monitoring) before saving assessments.
  7. Review the records and reports before deciding on the next support.

Offline use and learner data protection

Passages and built-in word meanings are packaged with the app, so regular use does not need internet. Speech depends on the voices installed on the device. Teacher-added words, learner records, names and game scores are stored on the device only and do not synchronise automatically. Back up regularly, and keep files with learner information secure in line with the Data Privacy Act. Turn learner names off in School & Print before sharing printouts.

Our guiding principle

Educating a child is a shared responsibility. Reading grows when learners have good stories, time to practise, someone to listen and a community that cares. e-BASA puts one more reading helper in the learner’s hands.

    Research & intervention evaluation pre-test and post-test

    Uses each learner’s first Pre-test and latest Post-test (set the Stage when saving an assessment). It computes means, medians, modes, standard deviations, gains, a paired-samples t-test and Cohen’s d. The interpretation is a draft: the app shows measured change, not proof that e-BASA caused it.

    To make a PDF in a browser, choose “Save as PDF” as the printer in the Print window.

    Report Center printable reports

    In a browser, choose “Save as PDF” as the printer to make a PDF. Reports use learner codes, not names, to protect learner privacy.

    How e-BASA monitors oral reading

    For each grade, e-BASA marks one passage as the Pre-test / Post-test passage. The learner reads it aloud at the start (pre-test), practises with the other passages, and reads the same passage again later (post-test). While the learner reads, the teacher times the reading and marks every miscue on a copy of the passage, then records the totals in Assess a Learner. The teacher can also use any other passage for a progress check.

    1. Give the learner a copy of the passage. Keep your own copy to mark.
    2. Start the timer when the learner starts reading aloud.
    3. Mark each miscue as shown below. Do not count self-corrections.
    4. Stop the timer. Count the miscues by type and add them up.
    5. Ask the comprehension questions shown in the assessment screen and record the number answered correctly.
    6. Compute the oral reading score and the reading speed (this screen does it for you).

    Marking and scoring the miscues

    MiscueHow to mark itExampleHow to score it

    Every miscue has equal weight, whether or not it changes the meaning of the passage. These are common oral reading miscue categories.

    Oral reading score

    (Number of words − number of miscues) ÷ number of words × 100

    Example: 65 words, 15 miscues → (65 − 15) ÷ 65 × 100 = 76.9%.

    Reading levelWord reading score
    ✅ Independent97–100%
    🟡 Instructional90–96%
    🔴 Frustration89% and below

    Reading speed

    Words read ÷ reading time in seconds × 60 = words per minute

    Example: 103 words in 90 seconds → 103 ÷ 90 × 60 = 68.6, or 69 words per minute.

    Reading levelSpeed profile
    ✅ Independent90 and above
    🟡 Instructional70–89
    🔴 Frustration69 and below

    Notes for teachers

    • The score levels and the speed profile above are commonly used oral reading benchmarks in Philippine schools. If your school or division requires different cut-offs, follow that guidance when you interpret the results.
    • The word count is counted from the passage text and can be edited. If the learner did not finish the passage, enter the number of words actually read.
    • The comprehension questions have suggested answers. Accept other sensible answers, especially for the critical-thinking questions.
    • These tools record and calculate. The teacher remains responsible for administering the assessment, interpreting results and deciding on support.

    🧒 Learner Reading Station

    For a computer that learners use on their own during free time. When station mode is ON, each learner signs in with a learner code before reading. The app records the minutes, passages and games for each learner. The Teacher Corner stays locked with your PIN.

    🎟 Game Pass games are a reward for reading

    Learners earn a Game Pass by reading stories and finishing the Comprehension Check. Each pass opens one limited game round (default: 3 stars, at most 10 questions, 3 rounds a day per learner, and a 5-minute time limit). Spending stars lowers the number of stars to spend, but never the learner’s total stars or reading rank.

      💡 How to play and learn

      1. Type the word in Word Helper, or tap a word in a passage.
      2. Press SPEAK. Use SLOW if needed.
      3. Listen, repeat the word, then read it in the sentence.
      4. Save a difficult word to practise again later.
      For classroom use: connect speakers or headphones. The voice depends on the voices installed on the computer/browser. Test it before learners use the station.
